100.q: Clock times in the flight plan form are inserted as:

ex.9: CH = MH − easterly deviation = 132 − 4 = 128°. TH = MH − westerly variation = 132 − 24 = 108°.
ex.17: Accelerating on a westerly heading in the northern hemisphere gives an apparent turn towards north; on 270° that means a reading above 270°, i.e. over-reading.
ex.22: 36 000 ft / 6076 ft per NM ≈ 5.92 NM of slant range.
ex.33: QDM 050 → QDR (radial) 230° M. The VOR phase difference equals the radial: 230°.
ex.39: In the southern hemisphere the great circle from B westwards starts south of west: 270 − 266 = 4° = half the convergency, so convergency = 8° = Δlong × sin 30° → Δlong = 16°. B = 12 + 16 = 028° E.
ex.40: QTE (true radial) 220° + 10° W = 230° M, which equals the phase difference.
ex.50: 80 kN × 0.6 kg/(s·kN) = 48 kg/s × 3600 s = 172 800 kg (as the question's units give).
ex.54: Based on the reduced TAS: O = 130 kt, H = 170 kt. CP = 1200 × 170 / 300 = 680 NM; at the normal GS of 180 kt that takes about 3 h 46 min.
ex.55: Wind component on 090° = −30 cos 120° = +15 kt (tail). On 3 engines O = 315, H = 285: CP = 1500 × 285 / 600 ≈ 712 NM; at the 4-engine GS of 375 kt that takes ≈ 1 h 54 min.
ex.60: GS out ≈ 224 kt, home ≈ 254 kt; endurance = 900 / 150 = 6 h. TPNR = 6 × 254 / 478 ≈ 3.19 h = 3 h 11 min; DPNR ≈ 714 NM.
ex.62: CP = D × H / (O + H): more tailwind out raises O and lowers H, so the CP moves closer to the start.
ex.63: QNH is 5 hPa above standard: indicated altitude ≈ 5000 + 5 × 30 = 5150 ft.
ex.64: Book key prints (c). The ionospheric delay is the largest atmospheric error in GNSS ranging (tropospheric delay is smaller), so the correct answer is (b).
ex.70: Range resolution = c × PW / 2 = 300 m/µs × 0.5 / 2 = 75 m.
ex.76: Track is left of heading: 3° port drift. Ground vector − air vector gives a wind of about 287°/39 kt.
ex.77: TMG = heading + starboard drift = 094°. To correct a 9° starboard track error the required track is 094 − 9 = 085°.
ex.81: At 000° longitude LMT = UTC, so the flight takes 2 h 30 min: 500 / 2.5 = 200 kt.
ex.91: Full scale ≈ 0.7° above or below, so 2 dots ≈ 0.35°. At 3 NM: 3 × 6076 × tan 0.35° ≈ 111 ft; fly-up means the aircraft is below.
ex.93: Closing angle = 15 NM over the remaining 135 NM ≈ 15/135 × 60 ≈ 7°.
ex.97: With 060 set the aircraft (on radial 235) is 5° from the 240 radial and TO shows. Facing 060 the aircraft is right of course, so the needle is half-scale left (5° of a 10° scale).
